boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Jonesborough record (August 31-September 1, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. The Union movement from August 25, the evacuation of Atlanta on the night of September 1 and the Lovejoy's Station positions are context. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields read Six corps [US] and two corps [CS] without counts; the live field reads zero. Hardee says two Union corps were in position on the 31st with a third in reserve and three more in support, that on September 1 six corps under Sherman attacked his single corps, which held in single rank the line of two corps, and that three of Lee's brigades arrived late on the 31st; he says Hood believed only two Union corps were at Jonesborough. Cox says the attackers on the 31st were mostly of Lee's corps.
claims.rationale: Corps counts, not personnel; the Confederate force changed overnight when Lee's corps was recalled. None is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.rationale: Stated aims from interested accounts and a summary; not a causal estimate.

claims.value: Hardee says he urged Hood to come and take command on the 31st, and that Atlanta fell from Hood's misconception of Sherman's plans, not from the battle. Cox says Cleburne commanded Hardee's corps, and that Stanley's delay kept the Fourth Corps from deploying before dark on September 1 despite Sherman's and Thomas's efforts. The frozen commanders are Lieutenant General William J. Hardee and Major General William T. Sherman; the live page gives General William Sherman and Lieutenant General William Hardee.
claims.rationale: Attributed judgments in a Hardee-Hood controversy and an interested history; Hood, Lee, Cleburne and Stanley are not listed commanders; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and the live ranks are not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Hardee reported the 31st as without decisive results, Lee having been badly repulsed; on September 1 he says the assault was repulsed except where Lewis's and Govan's brigades gave way, and that he retired four miles at night once the evacuation was secured. Cox says Govan and most of his brigade with two batteries were captured. NPS says Hood evacuated Atlanta that night and Sherman cut the supply line but failed to destroy Hardee's command.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The evacuation of Atlanta is campaign context, not the tactical result.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty texts read 3,149 (US 1,149; CS 2,000). For September 1 Cox gives Union losses of 371 in Carlin's division, 330 in Este's brigade and about the same in Morgan's division, over 300 Confederate dead left on the field, 865 surrendered with Govan and nearly a thousand more captured next day; for the 31st he says over four hundred Confederate dead were left. Hardee reported a few prisoners and 8 guns lost and a loss not heavy in killed and wounded on September 1, and quotes Hood's 1,400 killed and wounded for the attack of the 31st, chiefly in Lee's corps. Hardee also quotes Hood's total of 5,247 for July 18 through Jonesborough and says his own corps alone lost considerably more than 7,000.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Hood's 5,247 and Hardee's 7,000 are period totals (context), not assigned to this record. Cox's components are partial and span two days.

open_questions: Hood's report (a family for other records), S. D. Lee's report, Cleburne's division reports (Lowrey, Govan, Granbury), Howard's, Logan's, Davis's and Stanley's reports and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Hardee's telegrams of August 31-September 3, 1864 and his April 5, 1865 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, are a third family (interested Confederate accounts, written in controversy with Hood). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
